## Day 046 · lang-cpp — POSIX sockets, or Boost.Asio, and one thread per connection

Source: [`days/day-046-binary-search-on-the-answer/07-lang-cpp-posix-sockets-or-boost.md`](../../days/day-046-binary-search-on-the-answer/07-lang-cpp-posix-sockets-or-boost.md)

- A socket is an `int` file descriptor; every call returns `-1` on failure and sets `errno`. Check it.
- `socket` → fill `sockaddr_in` with `htons` and `inet_pton` → `bind` (with the `sockaddr*` cast) → `listen` → loop `accept`.
- `accept` returns a new descriptor per client; the listener never carries data.
- `std::thread(serve_one, client).detach()`; a `jthread` here joins and stalls the accept loop.
- `read` returns 0 on hang-up; then `close(client)`, or the leak ends in `accept: Too many open files`.

## Day 046 · lang-go — net.Listen, Accept, and one goroutine per connection

Source: [`days/day-046-binary-search-on-the-answer/06-lang-go-net-listen-accept-and.md`](../../days/day-046-binary-search-on-the-answer/06-lang-go-net-listen-accept-and.md)

- `net.Listen("tcp", "host:port")` is socket + bind + listen; it returns a `net.Listener`.
- `Accept()` blocks and returns one `net.Conn` per client; the listener never carries bytes.
- `go handle(conn)` and straight back to `Accept`; without `go`, the second client hangs.
- `defer conn.Close()` first; `io.Copy(conn, conn)` is the whole echo and ends on `io.EOF`.
- `bind: address already in use` is the port taken; `connect: connection refused` is no server.

## Day 046 · lang-python — socket, bind, listen, accept, and a threaded echo server

Source: [`days/day-046-binary-search-on-the-answer/05-lang-python-socket-bind-listen-accept.md`](../../days/day-046-binary-search-on-the-answer/05-lang-python-socket-bind-listen-accept.md)

- `socket` → `bind(addr)` → `listen()` → loop on `accept()`.
- `accept` returns a **new** socket per client; the listener never carries data.
- `recv(n)` gives up to `n` bytes; empty means the client closed. Use `sendall`, not `send`.
- One thread per connection keeps `accept` free; blocking in the accept loop stalls every other client.
- `Address already in use` means bind lost; `Connection refused` means nobody is listening.
